video_title: 2027 Market Warning: Why We're Preparing for Quad 4
gist: Largely a promotional Cyber November webcast, but Keith McCullough states Hedgeye sees Q3 2026 as the growth-cycle peak and the first half of 2027 as 'definitively' Quad 4, and details a defensive rotation: 33-34% cash, long health care, staples, the US dollar and long-duration bonds (25-year zeros), out of software/semis, with the S&P newly bearish on trade and trend.

insights.claim: Keith McCullough says the first half of 2027 is 'pretty definitively' Quad 4, with both growth and inflation decelerating as the economy exits Quad 2.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Position defensively: bonds, staples, health care, dollar; underweight high-beta tech.
insights.quote: Well, Quad 4, when Quad 4? First half of 2027, that's pretty definitively Quad 4, okay?

insights.claim: McCullough says Q3 2026 will be seen as the peak of the growth cycle, and that inflation is about to come off its cycle peak after accelerating into December CPI.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Growth and inflation both rolling over supports duration longs.
insights.quote: Q3 of 2026 is going to be looked back at as the peak of the cycle.

insights.claim: McCullough claims the AI bubble peaked in Q2 2026 (May-June), with cyclicals such as industrials peaking in Q3.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Rotation away from AI/semis and cyclicals is underway.
insights.quote: there's a couple things like the AI bubble that peaked in Q2. Okay? In May and June.

insights.claim: The S&P 500 has newly turned bearish on both Hedgeye's trade and trend durations, which McCullough expects to persist as the market moves toward Quad 4.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Index-level signal flipped bearish; expect better short-side alpha.
insights.quote: now the S&P's bearish trade and trend which is new.

insights.claim: The commodities CRB index broke trade and trend, prompting Hedgeye to cut remaining commodity exposure, leaving oil at a minimum position.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Commodity momentum broken; reduce inflation-hedge exposure.

insights.claim: McCullough says gold, which peaked around $5,419 in Quad 1, gets hit in Quad 2 and is still signaling 'don't buy me yet' despite historically working in Quad 4.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Don't rush into gold on Quad 4 backtests alone.

themes.theme: Positioning: rotation to defensives and duration

insights.claim: Hedgeye's largest equity positions are health care and consumer staples, it holds a very large US dollar position, and it is waiting to buy utilities.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Classic Quad 4 defensive tilt.
insights.quote: Our biggest positions are health care and consumer staples right now

insights.claim: After being short fixed income, McCullough has started buying bonds, adding 25-year zero-coupon Treasuries (longer than TLT's 20-year), CAT bonds and JPMorgan Core Plus bonds.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Long-duration bonds favored into decelerating growth/inflation.

insights.claim: McCullough's long-only portfolio is about 33-34% cash, raised by selling positions that broke trend rather than targeting a cash level; high-yield cash and AAA CLO ETFs are the top holdings.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Elevated cash signals defensive stance.

insights.claim: Hedgeye exited software (IGV) after it broke trend and holds cybersecurity (BUG) only at minimum position on a short leash; it replaced QQQ with equal-weight RSP.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Equal-weight over cap-weight tech as megacap leadership fades.

insights.claim: Over the period cited, tech fell 11-12% while consumer staples rose about 12%, which McCullough uses to validate the rotation.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Defensive rotation already paying off.

insights.claim: Semiconductors are down 28% from their cycle peak, requiring a 39% gain to break even; Hedgeye was short semis as SOXL lost $10 billion of AUM in three days.
insights.speaker: Hedgeye host
insights.so_what: Leveraged semi products face outflows; semis in drawdown.

insights.claim: McCullough cites Oracle and Intel as stocks down 60-65% from where people chased them, warning that a 63% loss needs a 170% gain to break even.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Avoid bag-holding broken AI/tech trades.

insights.claim: Hedgeye's Signal Strength list has 46 longs and 68 shorts, recently flipped from mostly longs; names entering are staples, financials and lower beta, while SanDisk and Marvell have dropped off and shorts include Core Weave (CoreWeave) and AMAT.
insights.speaker: Hedgeye host
insights.so_what: Breadth of shorts in tech/AI names signals regime change.

insights.claim: Apple is the longest-held Signal Strength long, while Hedgeye is short most of the other 'Magnificent Seven' names; Apple may lose signal strength if weakness continues.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Apple is relative defensive within megacap tech.

insights.claim: On a Friday when the S&P fell 1.8%, McCullough says his long-only portfolio was up 0.04%.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Illustrates defensive positioning working.

themes.theme: Hedgeye process: rate of change and trade/trend/tail

insights.claim: Hedgeye's framework maps the rate of change of growth and inflation into four quads: Quad 1 Goldilocks, Quad 2 growth and inflation accelerating (bubbles, high beta), Quad 3 stagflation (commodities), Quad 4 both decelerating (bonds, defensives).
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Asset allocation keyed to second derivative of macro, not levels or valuation.

insights.claim: McCullough argues markets move on acceleration or deceleration rather than cheap versus expensive, so accelerating assets can get far more expensive than valuation experts expect.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Valuation alone is a poor timing tool.
insights.quote: It's about things accelerating or decelerating. That's what makes stocks, markets,

insights.claim: Hedgeye's trade/trend/tail durations are under 3 weeks, 3 months or more, and up to 3 years; a break of the immediate-term trade is not a dip to buy but the start of volatility breaking out.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Sell on trade breaks rather than buying dips.
insights.quote: When the trade breaks, one must stop buying because it's not a dip.

insights.claim: McCullough describes the market as dominated by systematic 'machine' flows since ETFs overtook hedge funds around 2013, with hedge funds trying to front-run what the machine buys next; Hedgeye uses Tier 1 Alpha flow and gamma data.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Flow/positioning data is key to short-term market moves.

insights.claim: McCullough's risk rules: per-asset min/max sizes (currency up to 12%, fixed income 10%, commodities 1-4%, equities 2-6%, single stocks 1-3%), sell into strength, cut losers down 3-7%, and 'sell all' when a name leaves the signal list.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Concrete position-sizing discipline for active managers.

insights.claim: McCullough says he has shown over 9,000 timestamped positions and has been wrong about 22% of the time.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Self-reported hit rate; marketing claim.
